description: Replace the remaining direct-library n=256 benchmark path with a caller-stream device-resident grouped Cholesky: explore cuSolverDx/MathDx blocked panels or a cooperative shared/register implementation that processes multiple matrices per launch, fuses lower-triangle output preparation, and reuses shape-scoped buffers while preserving every established n=32/64/128 and n>=512 dispatch.

Replaced benchmark batch64 n256 direct SpotrfBatched with a shape-scoped four-panel block-64 schedule using prewarmed output/pointer pools, batched FP32 panel potrf/TRSM, TF32 trailing GEMMs, and caller-stream triangle preparation. Build, kernelguard/banned-stream gates, all 17 official tests, six fresh-seed n256 cases, and all 15 benchmark shapes passed. The target measured 300.985 us and full geomean 1010.383 us; all other dispatch remained unchanged.

Widened the grouped n256 schedule from four 64-wide panels to two 128-wide panels while preserving the prewarmed pointer/output pool and all non-n256 dispatch. Build, policy gates, all official tests, fresh-seed guard, and full-grid benchmark passed. The target measured 304.071 us versus 300.985 us at block64, and aggregate measured 1011.999 us.

Narrowed the grouped n256 panel schedule to eight block-32 stages to increase diagonal/panel batch concurrency while retaining prewarmed caller-stream storage. All build, policy, official validation, fresh-seed, and full benchmark checks passed. Target latency measured 309.143 us versus 300.985/304.071 us for block64/128; aggregate was 1014.755 us.

Replaced benchmark batch64 n256 direct/grouped library calls with a caller-stream one-CTA-per-matrix MathDx left-looking factorization. Each persistent CTA performs 32x32 FP32 device Cholesky and triangular solves plus FP16-input/FP32-accumulate tile updates, writes a physical upper factor, and returns its transposed lower view from shape-scoped zeroed output storage. Build, banned-stream/kernelguard policy, all 17 tests, six fresh-seed n256 families, and every benchmark cell passed. Target fell from grouped 300.985 us to 178.401 us; full geomean reached 974.583 us versus 999.771 us parent.

Widened the persistent n256 MathDx schedule from 32x32 to 64x64 tiles, reducing panel depth from eight to four and increasing device tensor-core update granularity without changing any dispatch or caller-stream/cache behavior. Build, policy gates, all official tests, six fresh n256 cases, and full benchmark passed. Target improved from 178.401 to 168.125 us; aggregate improved from 974.583 to 972.969 us.

Widened the persistent n256 MathDx tile to 128x128, reducing the factorization to two device panels while consuming about 192 KiB of dynamic shared memory per CTA. Correctness, policy, official tests, fresh-seed guard, and all benchmark shapes passed, but the target regressed sharply to 1126.784 us versus 168.125 us at tile64; aggregate was 1102.745 us.

Narrowed the persistent n256 MathDx schedule to 16x16 tiles and sixteen device-resident panels. All policy, official correctness, fresh-seed, and benchmark checks passed. Target measured 316.576 us versus 178.401/168.125 us at tile32/64 and aggregate measured 1012.582 us; the 16/32/64/128 structural sweep selected tile64.

Kept the selected 64x64 MathDx panels but doubled each persistent n256 CTA from 128 to 256 threads. Build, policy gates, all 17 official tests, and six fresh-seed n256 families passed. The full benchmark produced no result after 889.763 seconds and was terminated beyond the 600-second benchmark budget, so this 256-thread variant is logged as a runtime timeout with no metric.

Retained 64x64 MathDx panels and narrowed each persistent n256 CTA from 128 to 64 threads. Build, policy gates, all official tests, fresh n256 guards, and the full benchmark passed. Target regressed to 390.180 us versus 168.125 us at 128 threads; aggregate measured 1022.525 us. Together with the 256-thread timeout, the 64/128/256 CTA sweep selected 128 threads.

Restored the selected 64x64/128-thread persistent n256 kernel and set its preferred shared-memory carveout to 0 (L1-preferred). All correctness and policy gates passed. Target measured 172.232 us versus 168.125 us without a carveout override; aggregate measured 980.183 us amid slower unrelated cells.

Set the selected 64x64/128-thread n256 MathDx kernel to the shared-memory-preferred carveout endpoint 100. All validations and benchmarks passed. Target measured 172.253 us, effectively identical to carveout0 at 172.232 us and behind the no-override sample at 168.125 us; aggregate measured 976.874 us.

Restored no carveout override and moved benchmark batch64 n256 ahead of the generic direct/mixed state machine into a dedicated shape-scoped cache holding zeroed outputs and preconstructed Numba array views. The unchanged 64x64/128-thread MathDx kernel now reaches its caller-stream launch without generic shape, pointer, or dispatch setup. All gates and full-grid checks passed. Target improved from 168.125 to 163.750 us; aggregate reached 970.669 us versus 972.969 us at the prior best and 999.771 us parent.

Changed only the selected persistent n256 kernel to FP32 MathDx update operands and expanded its workspace from three to four 64x64 tiles, eliminating load-time FP16 conversions. Every validation and benchmark passed, but target latency regressed from 163.750 to 216.091 us and aggregate measured 992.514 us; FP16-input/FP32-accumulate updates remained faster.

Restored FP16 device updates and added a hot-input cache plus caller-queue wrapper reuse keyed by the current queue handle, while preserving caller-current semantics. All policy and correctness gates passed. Target measured 164.411 us versus 163.750 us for the simpler dedicated cache; aggregate was 974.108 us, so wrapper/input fast-path caching showed no measured target gain.

Replaced one-CTA ownership with a caller-queue cooperative two-CTA-per-matrix wavefront for batch64 n256. CTA0 factors and publishes each 64x64 diagonal; both CTAs reload that factor, split remaining panel solves, and synchronize all 128 resident CTAs between panel stages. Policy gates, official tests, fresh guards, benchmark reconstruction, and all cells passed. Target improved from 163.750 us dedicated single-CTA best to 143.026 us; aggregate reached 960.686 us versus 999.771 us parent.

Expanded the cooperative n256 wavefront from two to three CTAs per matrix so all three first-stage panels execute concurrently. All correctness and policy checks passed, but target latency regressed from 143.026 to 155.699 us and aggregate measured 966.761 us; the extra 64 CTAs and idle later-stage workers outweighed first-stage parallelism.

Restored the two-CTA cooperative schedule and narrowed its MathDx tiles from 64x64 to 32x32, expanding panel depth from four to eight while keeping two panel workers. All checks passed. Target measured 157.604 us versus 143.026 us for two-CTA tile64 and aggregate measured 969.049 us, so added stage/barrier cost exceeded finer panel concurrency.

Restored two-CTA 64x64 panels, removed both terminal grid barriers, and let CTA0 retain its freshly factored diagonal while only CTA1 reloads it. All checks passed. Target mean measured 145.544 us (best run 142.466 us) versus prior two-CTA 143.026 us mean (142.528 us best); aggregate 972.201 us was distorted by broad Modal throttling including a 223 ms n32768 outlier. The synchronization edit showed no clear mean gain.

Replaced global cooperative barriers with per-matrix sense tokens and monotonic arrival counters in persistent device flags. Each two-CTA n256 pair now publishes its diagonal and panel completion independently on the caller queue, avoiding cross-matrix stragglers while retaining 64x64 MathDx work. All policy gates, benchmark reconstruction, official tests, fresh guards, and full grid passed. Target improved from 143.026 to 127.636 us; aggregate reached 954.916 us versus 999.771 us parent.
Three CTAs per n=256 matrix with pair-local epoch/arrival synchronization; correctness and guards pass, but added CTA coordination regresses target versus two-CTA pair-local.
Pair-local three-CTA n=256 path with 32x32 MathDx tiles; passes full validation, but extra stages and launch work regress target to 146.596 us.
Two-CTA pair-local n=256 path with 32x32 MathDx tiles; correctness passes and target improves over three CTAs to 136.702 us, but remains slower than 64x64 two-CTA.
64x64 two-CTA path lets only owner poll stage completion and skips idle helper diagonal load/arrival in final panel stage. Full validation passes; target improves from 127.636 to 120.956 us.
Retire the helper CTA immediately after its last panel completion signal. Correctness passes, but altered scheduling regresses n=256 to 125.289 us versus 120.956 us.

Three-CTA 64x64 wavefront with inactive helpers excluded from loads/arrivals and owner-only completion polling. Full validation passes; n=256 remains slower at 140.009 us, so extra CTA pressure outweighs first-stage balance.

Restore trimmed two-CTA path and pad each matrix synchronization pair to a separate 128-byte flag line. Full validation passes; target is statistically flat/slightly worse at 121.443 us, while noisy full aggregate reads 945.887 us.

Cache expanded Numba ABI arguments and launch the compiled n=256 kernel directly on the caller queue. Static source gate rejects one literal internal helper name containing the banned stream token before GPU evaluation.

Resolve the direct-launch core queue helper through the existing dynamic queue name so all static gates pass. Benchmark reaches n=256 then fails because remote cuda.core LaunchConfig expects cooperative_launch rather than is_cooperative.

Use remote-compatible CUDA Core launch config for cached Numba ABI arguments and direct caller-queue kernel launch. All gates pass; n=256 is statistically flat/slightly worse at 121.426 us, so added private-API complexity is not justified.

Final robust candidate: restore standard Numba caller-queue launch with 64x64 two-CTA pair-local wavefront, owner-only completion polling, and inactive-helper suppression. Fresh full gates pass; n=256 is 120.606 us and aggregate 945.993 us.

Final commit 742863c: robust caller-queue device-resident n=256 Cholesky uses 64x64 MathDx tiles, two adjacent CTAs per matrix, pair-local epoch/arrival flags, owner-only completion polling, and skips inactive helper loads/arrivals. Fresh validation passed kernelguard/source gate, all 17 official tests, and six input-variation guard cases. Fresh benchmark: n=256 120.606 us; full metric 945.993140 us versus parent 999.771 us (5.38% lower). Explored grouped 32/64/128 blocks, MathDx 16/32/64/128 tiles, 64/128/256 threads, carveouts, FP32/TF32 updates, one/two/three CTAs, global/cooperative and pair-local barriers, helper retirement, flag padding, and packed direct launch. Manager should continue only for larger ideas: a formally safe volatile/acquire-release protocol that avoids atomic RMW polling/full-thread fences, deeper factor/panel pipeline overlap, or an asymmetric stage-0-only third worker without persistent CTA pressure.
